industry.summary: Chained quick-service restaurants (QSR) are a small slice of Indian food spending. JFL's FY26 presentation (citing industry reports) sizes India's chained QSR market at ~US$3.2 bn in 2024 growing to ~US$5.4 bn by 2028 (~14% a year), with chains at ~6% of a ~US$60 bn foodservice market (US ~US$800 bn, China ~US$760 bn). Delivery is the growth channel: food aggregators cut minimum order values to Rs99 and then Rs49, which pulled small, solo orders away from dine-in and takeaway and forced Domino's to match (Rs149 to Rs99). Listed rivals: Westlife (McDonald's West & South), Devyani (KFC, Pizza Hut, Costa) and Sapphire (KFC, Pizza Hut) - both Yum franchisees - and Restaurant Brands Asia (Burger King India). KFC (Devyani, Sapphire) is the fried-chicken incumbent Popeyes is attacking. Most listed rivals made losses or near-zero profit in FY26 as same-store sales fell.
industry.dominosShare: Domino's gained ~80 bp of delivery share among the top 25 QSR brands year on year in Q1FY27 (NielsenIQ, per the Q1FY27 letter); JFL calls itself the largest QSR player for 30 years, ~1.7x the second largest (FY26 presentation).
industry.turkey: DP Eurasia runs 787 Domino's stores in Turkey, Azerbaijan and Georgia and COFFY is the 5th largest coffee brand in Turkey by stores (194). Turkey has been hyperinflationary under IAS 29 since 2022; Domino's Turkey LFL was +30.6% in lira but -1.3% after inflation in Q1FY27.

excluded.RBA: Restaurant Brands Asia's consolidated EBITDA was negative or near zero (Indonesia losses) from Oct-2021 to May-2022, so Screener has no EV/EBITDA for 35 of the 261 weeks: no complete five-year median (the pharma precedent drops peers with loss years inside the window). Shown as a sensitivity row.

peers.note: QSR set (natural peers; same customers, delivery aggregators and landlords). The valuation metric is EV/EBITDA, on which Westlife, Devyani and Sapphire have positive EBITDA through the whole window, so their five-year EV/EBITDA medians are usable; their net profits are tiny or negative, so their P/E histories are not, and the P/E cross-check uses the retail set fixed in DMART.ctx.js (DMART, TRENT, METROBRAND, BATAINDIA, PAGEIND). Sapphire listed 18-Nov-2021 and misses the first 7 weeks of the window (Metro Brands precedent in the retail set). Three usable QSR peers: a thin set, so the retail set's EV/EBITDA move is shown as a sensitivity row. Devyani and Sapphire agreed to merge on 1-Jan-2026 (177 Devyani shares for 100 Sapphire; Business Today, 2-Jan-2026, https://www.businesstoday.in/markets/stocks/story/sapphire-foods-merger-here-is-fresh-target-price-for-devyani-international-509053-2026-01-02); both still traded separately on 30-Sep-2026, so since January their prices move together.

governance.capitalAllocation: DP Eurasia bought for ~Rs770 cr for the stake added in FY24 (plus the earlier ~33% holding); Dunkin' exited and Hong's not funded further (management: 'painful' capital-allocation calls); supply-chain capex now past its peak.

moat.why: 2,455 Domino's stores in 540 cities, own rider fleet (45,000+ partners), 20-minute delivery; 76% of Domino's revenue is delivery, mostly on its own app (19.5 mn monthly active users across brands).
Commissaries sized for ~5,000 stores after the Mumbai plant; lowest-ever supply-chain cost (Q4FY26 call).
Gross margin 75%+, but Domino's had to match aggregators' Rs99 minimum order and LFL slowed from 11.6% to 0.2% in four quarters.
Domino's and Popeyes are licensed (royalties to Domino's Pizza Inc. and RBI); the master-franchise agreements are long-dated but not owned.

critiques: Domino's LFL fell from 11.6% (Q1FY26) to 0.2% (Q4FY26) and 2.5% (Q1FY27) while stores grew ~12%: revenue per store is falling.
Reported EBITDA excludes rent; after rent the standalone margin was 12.6% in FY26, and the +200 bp target set at the 2025 Investor Day now runs to end-FY28.

Turkey's rupee profits depend on IAS 29 monetary gains and the lira, and come with minorities (6.35% of DP Eurasia). Most of the group's Rs1,745 cr of bank debt is euro acquisition debt for DP Eurasia (two term loans of Jubilant FoodWorks Netherlands, EUR 45.6 mn + EUR 64 mn = Rs1,183 cr, guaranteed by the parent; AR FY26 note 16), so a weaker rupee raises it.
Return on capital is modest: Screener ROCE 15% in FY26 (company standalone pre-Ind AS ROCE 18.9%).
